correctness.rationale: For m≥2, all-positive completion forces every size-m support to be an entire perfect matching, precluding single-negative traces. The constructive induction avoids at most r−1 disjoint boundary edges on 2r vertices; fixed positives reduce the target to this lemma. For a top-dimensional shattered support containing a diagonal, the sole unused matching edge lies on one side and a distinct support edge on the other is forced under its single-negative trace, contradiction. Conversely all near-perfect boundary matchings shatter. Two uncovered opposite-parity vertices determine the unique boundary completion, giving m². Independently generated full Catalan families and exhaustive top-support traces agree for m≤6. Computations are supplemental, not infinite proof.

evidence: Sheyn–Tessler (2011) states that any r−1 edge deletions from a complete geometric graph on 2r vertices preserve a noncrossing perfect matching; this supplies the positive shattering construction after fixing required boundary edges.
Keller–Perles (2009 preprint) characterizes minimum m-edge blocking sets as caterpillars and counts m·2^(m−1) blockers, not fully shattered near-perfect matchings.
Milich–Mütze–Pergel (2020) Theorems 3–5 count/characterize centered-flip vertex degrees, not complete trace realizability.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Known edge-removal results dominate only the existence lemma for all negative traces, including after shrinking by positive boundary pairs; they do not imply the necessity of boundary geometry for m−1 positive-query supports. Minimum blockers are hitting sets meeting every concept, whereas shattering requires a matching for each one of 2^(m−1) patterns. Degrees of flip-graph vertices count local replacements, not all patterns. General graph VC dimension results on different set systems do not settle the restricted convex matching classification.

value.rationale: A complete natural classification of the top-dimensional faces of the shattered-support complex for a classical Catalan hypothesis family is given for all polygon sizes, with a sharp VC dimension and an exact labeled m² count. The necessity of boundary edges is a structural rigidity result not supplied by generic avoidance bounds. The result singles out a meaningful geometric extreme rather than an arbitrary finite slice; it motivates lower-face topology and online-dimension questions without asserting them.
